headlines.title: Saudi Arabia Halts Energy Sites as Houthis Claim New Attacks
headlines.summary: This is the real deal, folks — Houthi strikes shutting Saudi energy facilities with Brent knifing toward $100 is a five-alarm fire for the tape. Energy stocks catch a bid, airlines and industrials get hit, and every inflation-sensitive name on the board has to reprice. With the Fed already eyeing another hike, an oil shock is the last thing this market needs heading into CPI week.

headlines.title: US Stock Market: Wall Street braces for CPI test as Fed rate-hike bets hang in balance
headlines.summary: Hot jobs data already has the Street sweating a September hike, and now the CPI print is the main event — every bond trader, equity desk, and rate-sensitive sector is holding its breath. A hotter-than-expected number could reprice the long bond fast and put real pressure on growth and rate-sensitive names. This is the macro catalyst that sets the tone for the whole week.

headlines.title: Canada's retaliatory tariffs worth $27.6 billion take effect as trade rift with U.S. deepens
headlines.summary: Canada just doubled steel and aluminum duties to 50% on U.S. goods — that's not a warning shot, that's a broadside. U.S. steel and aluminum producers get a short-term bid, but downstream manufacturers eating higher input costs are going to feel this in margins. With Bombardier already in the crosshairs and $27.6 billion on the table, this trade spat is moving from noise to real economic drag.
